QUESTION: Which service objectives can be measured, and at what cost?
     PROMPT: DIAGRAM: Title: Match service objectives to available evidence. Use five independent horizontal
     outcome cards on a taller canvas, with cost-category chips beside the available measurements.
     This replaces the cramped four-column matrix. Categories are parallel, never steps or a maturity
     ladder. Show only the following supported pairings; do not fill gaps with invented proxies.
     Administrative access: Cheap / direct, Request success and latency.
     Agent reporting: Cheap / partial, Oldest check-in in a filterable population.
     Device-management delivery: Cheap / partial, Queue age from one host's own view; Expensive,
     Estate-wide queue age requires enumeration.
     Scheduled processing: Not available, Supported current schedule-status surface.
     Data freshness: Cheap / partial, Maximum staleness: one ordered read in a filterable population;
     Expensive, Share past an arbitrary age: enumerate the population.
     Explain the distinction beneath these rows: Maximum age needs one ordered read; a share needs
     enumeration. There is no staleness-threshold filter. A small disconnected Fleet health check box
     contains only Database + Redis. It must not enclose, connect to, or govern any service-outcome card.
     Do not add per-node attribution or claim an estate-wide age filter exists.
     TERMINOLOGY: Fleet is the company, product, or server. Host groups are lowercase
     fleet/fleets, including headings and labels. Do not call these groups teams. Preserve
     exact code/API identifiers. These instructions are not text to render.
     DESIGN: Flat vector technical diagram. Fleet is software for managing computers; draw no
     vehicles. Use Inter labels and Roboto Mono identifiers. At 1400 px source width use 48 px
     titles, 36 px body labels, and at least 28 px secondary text; scale proportionally. Check at
     720 px reading width and intended print size. Use a 32 px spacing grid, at least 24 px node
     padding, and consistent corner radii. Center short node names; left-align multiline
     explanations. Never shrink text to fit. Use #F9FAFC background, #192147 headings and primary
     connectors, #515774 text, #8B8FA2 secondary connectors, #C5C7D1 borders, and #D3E8F3 or #E8F1F6
     quiet fills. Use #5CABDF and #C98DEF for named categories, #3AEFC4 for labelled positive
     outcomes, #D66C7B for labelled failures, and #FAA669 for labelled cautions. Tint large panels
     to 20 to 25 percent; full strength is for small marks. Keep text navy or slate, or off-white on
     a navy anchor. Never rely on colour alone. Use one arrowhead shape, consistent stroke weights,
     box-edge termination, and labelled branches and return paths. Keep connectors clear of text. No
     gradients, shadows, decorative icons, logo, watermark, em-dashes, or slogan footer. Render only
     the specified reader-facing labels. Choose orientation to fit the relationship, not a default
     poster. Keep captions outside the artwork. If labels crowd, split the figure before shrinking
     them. Keep editable SVG when the production method supports it.

WHY: The tall sequence consumes space without locating the recovery boundary or showing which writes a database restore loses.
     PROMPT: Explain recovery after a Fleet upgrade. Title: "Upgrade recovery and the backup point".
     Use a compact landscape canvas with a top timeline and a lower recovery decision, not a tall poster.
     The timeline is labelled "Documented offline upgrade; schematic, not to scale". In order show
     "Backup", "Stop all instances", "Apply migrations once", "Start new version", "New writes".
     Mark the migration point with a vertical rule labelled "Database state changes". Do not label
     it as the instant rollback becomes impossible: compatibility determines whether binary rollback is safe.
     Below the timeline put a decision "Have any migrations applied?". Branch "No" to "Restore old binary".
     Branch "Yes" to "Compatibility established for all applied migrations and subsequent writes?".
     From that question branch "Yes" to "Binary rollback may be possible" and "Not established" to
     "Restore pre-migration database backup". Do not treat a warning or a successful startup as a
     compatibility check. This is a recovery decision aid, not a command to execute a restore now.
     Draw a labelled dashed connector from the restore outcome back to the Backup point:
     "Returns database to this snapshot". Use an apricot bracket from Backup through New writes,
     labelled "Writes after this backup are lost if you restore it". Keep the bracket distinct from
     the serving timeline; do not imply Fleet keeps accepting writes while every instance is stopped.
     End both recovery outcomes with a shared short note "Repeat service acceptance checks".
     Do not include a generic lesson footer or imply that restoring the binary alone reverses migrations.
     TERMINOLOGY: Fleet is the company, product, or server. Host groups are lowercase
     fleet/fleets, including headings and labels. Do not call these groups teams. Preserve
     exact code/API identifiers. These instructions are not text to render.

     Use Inter for labels and Roboto Mono for literal identifiers. On a 1400 px wide canvas use
     48 px titles, 36 px body labels, and at least 28 px secondary text; scale proportionally.
     Check the raster at 720 px wide and at its intended print size. Never shrink text to fit.
     Use a 32 px spacing grid, at least 24 px internal padding, and consistent corner radii.

     PROMPT: DIAGRAM: Title: Hand over the ongoing operating responsibilities. One small navy box Fleet
     URL + admin login points to a much larger bracketed group Standing obligations. The size contrast
     makes the point. Inside the larger group, five independent rows use one small blue dot each:
     Three stores, More than one can lose unrecoverable data; Expiring credentials, Renewal schedules
     belong to other organizations; Certificate rotation, Order preserves agent connectivity;
     Upgrades, The documented procedure stops service; Periodic jobs, Can stop without reporting an
     error. Use left-aligned labels and enough room for the explanations. These are selected operating
     obligations, not a sequence. Avoid a slogan footer, decorative icons, or a product UI appearance.
     TERMINOLOGY: Fleet is the company, product, or server. Host groups are lowercase
     fleet/fleets, including headings and labels. Do not call these groups teams. Preserve
     exact code/API identifiers. These instructions are not text to render.
     DESIGN: Flat vector technical diagram. Fleet is software for managing computers; draw no
     vehicles. Use Inter labels and Roboto Mono identifiers. At 1400 px source width use 48 px
     titles, 36 px body labels, and at least 28 px secondary text; scale proportionally. Check at
     720 px reading width and intended print size. Use a 32 px spacing grid, at least 24 px node
     padding, and consistent corner radii. Center short node names; left-align multiline
     explanations. Never shrink text to fit. Use #F9FAFC background, #192147 headings and primary
     connectors, #515774 text, #8B8FA2 secondary connectors, #C5C7D1 borders, and #D3E8F3 or #E8F1F6
     quiet fills. Use #5CABDF and #C98DEF for named categories, #3AEFC4 for labelled positive
     outcomes, #D66C7B for labelled failures, and #FAA669 for labelled cautions. Tint large panels
     to 20 to 25 percent; full strength is for small marks. Keep text navy or slate, or off-white on
     a navy anchor. Never rely on colour alone. Use one arrowhead shape, consistent stroke weights,
     box-edge termination, and labelled branches and return paths. Keep connectors clear of text. No
     gradients, shadows, decorative icons, logo, watermark, em-dashes, or slogan footer. Render only
     the specified reader-facing labels. Choose orientation to fit the relationship, not a default
     poster. Keep captions outside the artwork. If labels crowd, split the figure before shrinking
     them. Keep editable SVG when the production method supports it.
     NOTE: Layout and labels refined 2026-09-08 for readable collection artwork, against
     the current chapter. This editorial adaptation is not a new release verification.
     Preserve published artwork and prose until the final joint review. Do not mark IMAGE-OK yet.
     CANDIDATE: ../../research/visual-reviews/part-7/assets/7.7-what-is-handed-over.webp
     Rendered and inspected for the overnight batch; awaiting final joint review.
